package_info.why_malicious: The campaign leverages phishing emails and injected JavaScript skimmers to steal cPanel credentials and payment card data from victims. Attackers use fake security advisories to lure users to credential-harvesting sites and deploy Magecart-style skimmers on e-commerce checkout pages, exfiltrating sensitive information to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

execution_context.trigger: User clicks phishing link in email (user interaction)
execution_context.file_location: Phishing email and phishing website (fake cPanel login page hosted on non-cPanel domain)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Victims who clicked the malicious link were redirected to a phishing website asking for their cPanel credentials.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user clicks the phishing link in the email, the browser is redirected to a fake cPanel login page; the page collects entered credentials and transmits them via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The website impersonates a legitimate cPanel login page and is hosted on a non-official domain, specifically to harvest user credentials and transmit them to an external attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate security advisories do not direct users to enter credentials on non-official domains; credential collection should only occur on trusted, official cPanel sites, and credentials should never be sent to unverified third-party servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate password reset or login pages for cPanel, but only when hosted on official cPanel domains and using secure, verified connections.
key_indicators: Fake login page visually mimicking cPanel interface on a non-cPanel domain
Unsolicited email referencing urgent security issues and prompting credential entry
Credential collection form posts data to attacker-controlled endpoint
Domain registration and hosting details inconsistent with official cPanel infrastructure

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user visits an e-commerce checkout page (JavaScript executes in browser)
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript on e-commerce checkout pages (via homoglyph domain or within favicon file)
required_permissions: access to DOM (to read credit card input fields)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: A new credit card skimming campaign making use of homoglyph – domain lookalike – techniques has been connected to an existing Magecart threat group that utilizes the inter kit and favicon to hide skimming activity and lure a victim into purchasing on malicious websites.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, injected JavaScript code on the checkout page accesses credit card input fields in the DOM, collects the entered payment data, and sends it via obfuscated network requests to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in payment card data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The JavaScript is injected into checkout pages, surreptitiously reads sensitive payment fields, and exfiltrates the data to external domains controlled by the attacker, often using obfuscation and hiding within favicon files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce sites do not inject or obfuscate JavaScript that accesses payment fields and sends data to untrusted third-party domains; favicons should not contain executable JavaScript.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processing scripts may access payment fields, but only to transmit data to trusted, vetted payment processors and never via obfuscated or hidden code.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into checkout or payment pages
JavaScript code embedded in or loaded from favicon files
Network requests (POST or XHR) from checkout pages to attacker-controlled or lookalike domains
Use of homoglyph (lookalike) domains to evade detection
Access to and exfiltration of credit card data from DOM elements

attack_chain.action: Phishing email sent to cPanel users with a fake security advisory and malicious link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User clicks link and is redirected to phishing website.

attack_chain.action: Phishing website collects cPanel credentials entered by the victim.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's cPanel account.

attack_chain.action: Magecart skimmer JavaScript is injected into e-commerce checkout pages on homoglyph or lookalike domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Skimmer executes when user visits checkout page.

attack_chain.action: Skimmer reads credit card data from DOM and exfiltrates it to attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Phishing emails referencing urgent cPanel security advisories with links to non-official domains
Web pages mimicking cPanel login hosted on domains not owned by cPanel
JavaScript accessing payment or credit card fields in the DOM and sending data to external or suspicious domains
Obfuscated or hidden JavaScript payloads embedded in favicon files or third-party scripts on checkout pages
file_indicators: Injected or obfuscated JavaScript present in e-commerce checkout pages
Favicon files (e.g., favicon.ico) containing or loading JavaScript payloads
Phishing email templates referencing cPanel vulnerabilities and containing non-cPanel URLs
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from checkout pages to domains using homoglyphs or lookalike names resembling legitimate brands
POST or XHR requests from web pages to recently registered or unrecognized domains
Phishing sites hosted on domains with registration details inconsistent with official cPanel or e-commerce brands
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor inbound email for messages referencing urgent cPanel security issues and containing links to non-official domains. Flag login pages for sensitive services (such as cPanel) that are hosted on domains not owned by the legitimate provider. Scan e-commerce sites for injected or obfuscated JavaScript, especially within favicon files or third-party scripts, that accesses payment fields and initiates network requests to untrusted domains. Monitor network traffic for POST or XHR requests from checkout pages to domains not associated with legitimate payment processors or service providers, and investigate domains using homoglyph or lookalike techniques.
